**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **139** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 243dd3c6256673dc1a56f9419be03c397129f825` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `967cf2fadf12ff4d3fa0f43c1854701a99cffb4c` — the merge of head `9c3733f39b37bf9805ef4558c87474da9b01d316` into base `243dd3c6256673dc1a56f9419be03c397129f825`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 967cf2fadf12ff4d3fa0f43c1854701a99cffb4c && git checkout 967cf2fadf12ff4d3fa0f43c1854701a99cffb4c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 243dd3c6256673dc1a56f9419be03c397129f825 9c3733f39b37bf9805ef4558c87474da9b01d316 && git checkout -B drift-repro 243dd3c6256673dc1a56f9419be03c397129f825 && git merge --no-ff 9c3733f39b37bf9805ef4558c87474da9b01d316
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9c3733f39b37bf9805ef4558c87474da9b01d316`
Local-runs: none

PR #22673 for card #22627, branch `claude/issue-22627-screen-title-text-slot-judge`. The head is a merge of `origin/main` `243dd3c625` into `327c0cc2fb`; the net delta against `main` is the PR's 6 files (216 insertions, 39 deletions). Inputs read: the card body and all 5 comments (triage `6094869470`, unlock `6095432757`, claim `6095600078`, the two `os-dev-report`s `6096446823` and `6098004242`), the governing ruling `6093472708` on #22507, the PR body, the REST file list, the diff against `main`, the 35 check-runs on the head, and files at `origin/main` and at the head through `git show`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept-set change, one leaf: `flows.FLOW.screens.NODE_ID.title` narrows — right.** On `main` the leaf is `z.string().optional()`; at the head it is `flowTextSlotTranslation().optional()`, a `superRefine` over the one judge `textSlotTemplateRefusal`. That judge has two arms at the head (`singleBraceRefusal` and `unboundRootHoleRefusal`), so the leaf now refuses a single-brace `{token}` (the card's defect) and a `{{ }}` hole over a `$` root the engine does not bind (the arm stock changeset `22477` gave the judge). The ruling and the triage direction say the ONE judge and ⛔ not a second one, so the second arm riding along is by design, and the changeset's "What is refused" names both arms, so the narrowing is declared at its true width. The empty string stays accepted (pinned). The `.describe()` string of the leaf is unchanged. The narrowing reaches every door that embeds the shape: `TranslationDataSchema`, `TranslationItemSchema` (the metadata-item door, pinned), `PlatformTranslationDataSchema`, and the manifest and API schemas that embed them — the eight schemas the ledger names.
2. **`description` and `refusals.NODE_ID.message`: no accept-set change — right.** The factory is the inline `superRefine` moved, same judge, same `custom` issue, same `.optional().describe(...)` chain. A refactor with no contract movement; the family pin (`FLOW_SCREEN_COPY_KEYS` plus `message`, with a floor) holds all three on the one judge.
3. **Public surface: nothing new reaches it — right.** `flowTextSlotTranslation` is a module-level `const`, not exported, and its docblock says why. The test's imports (`TEXT_SLOT_TEMPLATE_REFUSAL`, `FLOW_SCREEN_COPY_KEYS`, `TranslationItemSchema`) already exist at `main`. The leaf's TS type does not move (`superRefine` keeps `ZodString`, so the leaf is ZodOptional of ZodString before and after). `packages/spec/api-surface/**` and `export-origins/**` are not in the file list, and `git diff --name-only origin/main...head` over those two directories is empty. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core` and the four `Type Check` runs are green on the head.
4. **Published JSON Schema projection — right.** A `superRefine` is dropped by `z.toJSONSchema`, so the published JSON Schema (gitignored, generated at publish) keeps its shape and the committed record of the gap is `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`. Read at the head: 223 schemas carry sites, 701 sites in all, 8 of them the new `...screens.valueType.title` site (Manifest, GetTranslationsResponse, the `options[1].manifest` form, PlatformTranslationBundle, PlatformTranslationData, TranslationBundle, TranslationData, TranslationItem); at `main` the same read gives 223, 693, 0. The totals block at the head says 223 and 701, so the merge round's hand resolution of the conflicting totals is verified by count, not taken on the dev's word.
5. **ADR-0087 ledger — right.** A D3 semantic entry `translation-flow-screen-title-text-slot-refused` under protocol 18 (`PROTOCOL_VERSION` is `18.0.0` at the head; the entry sits in `step18`), with no D2 conversion: a single-brace heading always drew as literal text on every route, so only the translator can say whether a hole was meant, which is ADR-0087's "cannot be converted; it goes to D3" case. The `registry.ts` diff is exactly that one entry inserted in id order between `translation-component-submit-label-retired` and `translation-per-app-settings-platform-only`; the dev reports `gen:migration-registry` byte-identical in both rounds, and the gate's `registered` disposition requires the id to resolve at the head AND be new in the diff, which it is. PR #22635's `18.flow-text-slot-single-brace-refused.ts` is untouched.
6. **Gap prose closed, nothing made false — right.** The `⚠️` paragraph recording the gap in the `flows` docblock is replaced; a grep of the head for "not judged" / "unjudged" finds no residue for this key in `packages/spec/src`, `content/docs` or the liveness ledger; `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx` already says both screen keys are `{{ }}` templates the server renders. No generated reference moved (none in the file list; the dev reports `check:generated` 15 of 15 current in both rounds).
7. **Reach — consistent.** The dev measured 8 translated headings judged, 0 refused, at both bases, with a positive control refusing 2 of 48 messages. A read of the four bundle files at the head finds no `title:` value carrying a single brace. `Test Core` 6 of 6 and the consumer suites are green, so no fixture flips.
8. **Governed surface — none.** None of the 6 paths is a `GOVERNED_SURFACES` row; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is green. The PR is a draft awaiting this record under the claim's own protocol (a contract-face narrowing is reviewed at this tier before enqueue), not under Tier S.
9. **Check-runs on the head: 32 success, 3 skipped, 0 failure.** The three skipped are `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate` and the opt-in `Packed-tarball smoke`, all path-gated by the `filter` job; no export is removed or renamed and `resolveFlowScreenTitle` is untouched, so the pin gate has nothing this diff could redden. `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, the `Type Check` family, `Test Core` and the Dogfood gates are all green.
10. **Branch history — clean.** Five commits, linear from `86da194919` with two merges of `origin/main` (`5fb1746611`, then `243dd3c625`); the PR's commit list matches the branch; no amend or force push; the head equals the PR head. Commit trailers are AGENTS.md's model-free pair.

### ② Semver level

- **The changeset matches what the diff publishes.** `.changeset/22627-flow-screen-title-translation-text-slot.md` grades `@objectstack/spec` only, and `packages/spec` is the only published package the diff moves. It carries the BREAKING banner, the FROM → TO table, the one-line fix, the measured reach, the ledger paragraph, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered translation-flow-screen-title-text-slot-refused`). No tombstone is owed: no key is removed or renamed.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right, in the PR body and the changeset alike.** Clause ② is "a new key on a published payload"; this PR adds none (the `title` key predates it), so `no` is the truthful value, and `(narrowing)` is the arm that makes it BREAKING under the closed pair. The card body and the triage spelled `yes (narrowing)`; the claim, which binds, spelled `no (narrowing)`, and the PR follows the claim and the truth. The guard's LEVEL axis reads `no` as `not-declared` and stands down; `Check Changeset` is green on the head.
- **`minor` with a BREAKING section, in pre mode — right.** `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s header states the launch-window convention: a breaking change ships as `minor`, the level is not the carrier, and the carriers are the BREAKING banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, both present here. Its RC exemption says that while `.changeset/pre.json` reads `mode: pre` (it does, tag `next`) the guard stands aside for a `major`; that ADMITS `major`, it does not demand it, and the workflow's WHICH LEVEL prose says the same. The pending stock on `main` at `243dd3c625` is split: spec accept-set narrowings graded `minor` with a BREAKING banner (`13458`, the `15206`/`15207` set, `21898`, `21982`, `22054`, `22088`, `22114`, `22149`, `22343`, `22443`, `22470`, `22477`, `22568`, `5082`, `9139`) and graded `major` (`11509`, the `19939` set, `22110`, `22158`, `22491`, `22502`, `22565`). The nearest sibling, `22477-flow-text-slot-dollar-root-refused` — the `$`-root arm of this very judge — is `minor`, `no (narrowing)`, BREAKING. And the line's version is already decided: `22080-v18-line-opens` and `22130-protocol-18` carry `@objectstack/spec: major`, the fixed group takes the highest bump, so the next release is `18.0.0-next.N` whatever this changeset grades; the level here carries no information, exactly as the header says of the window. Observation, not a finding: the stock carries two banner wordings for one convention ("under the launch-window convention" here and in `22477`; "as `major` on the v18 line" in `11509`). That is a stock-wide inconsistency for the maintainer to settle once, not this PR's defect.

### ③ Boundary flags

Open questions: none in either report. Every flag answered below; nothing escalates.

**Report 1 (`6096446823`), out-of-scope findings.**
- *`.changeset/22507-screen-copy-engine-pick-spec.md`'s last bullet ("A translated screen `title` is not judged by the text-slot rule yet") becomes false in the same release.* Answered, not blocking. The dev's changeset carries the counter-sentence "An earlier entry in this release says …; that describes the face before this change", which is the shape two entries in the pending stock already use (`22428-field-existence-every-spelling`, `22481-attached-block-served-rows`), so the compiled CHANGELOG reads correctly in order. The cleaner outcome is deleting that one bullet; it is outside the card's file surface, and the dev rightly noted it in the Acceptance notes rather than widening scope (Prime Directive #10). The seat may fold the one-line deletion into this PR before enqueue, or leave it to a follow-up; neither changes this verdict.
- *`AutomationEngine.renderFlowTextSlot`'s docblock hedge "for the keys that judge covers".* Answered, not blocking. Read at `main`: the sentence stays true (the judge now covers every key the engine picks), so the hedge is cosmetic residue, outside the surface; no issue is owed.

**Report 1, deviations.**
- *ADR-0087 D3 entry added after `check-adr-0087-registration` refused `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.* Right, and pre-authorised: the claim's file surface says "Only if `check-adr-0087-registration` demands one". The gate refuses `no-migration-prescription` on a changeset whose own body carries a FROM → TO, and AGENTS.md requires that FROM → TO on every breaking changeset, so `registered` was the only honest disposition; the triage's "ADR-0087 not required" was a prediction the gate overturned by measurement.
- *`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` against the card's `yes (narrowing)`.* Right; judged in ②.
- *Attribution trailers: AGENTS.md's model-free pair over the harness reminder.* Right; the commits carry `Claude-Session:` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`, the PR body ends with the session URL. Not a contract matter.
- *A never-pushed probe commit reset with `git reset --soft` onto the branch's own pushed commit.* Verified: the pushed history is the five commits above, no amend, no force push.
- *One pinned fixture commit fetched into the shared object store; the spec `repo` tier and a `--re-measure` turbo build run in the worktree.* Process only; objects without refs and a local run leave nothing in the diff.
- *`origin/main` merged before the PR opened.* Fine; the delta against `main` is the PR's 6 files.

**Report 2 (`6098004242`), the merge round.**
- *Head `9c3733f39b` is a merge, not a rebase.* Verified: parents `327c0cc2fb` and `243dd3c625`.
- *`dropped-refinements.baseline.json` totals resolved by counting the merged body.* Verified by an independent count at the head: 223 schemas, 701 sites, all 8 title sites present (①.4).
- *`registry.ts` auto-merged and regenerated byte-identical.* Consistent with the diff, which holds exactly the one new entry; `Build Core` and `Lint & Repo Gates` are green on the head.
- *The full 92-command gate battery is NOT MEASURED at `9c3733f39b`.* Answered by the head's check-runs: 32 success, 0 failure (①.9); the families the claim named are all green there.
- *Worktree re-created; two-step merge as the script prescribes.* Process only.
